Special Events Funding (City of Tacoma).notes: Latest cycle with a published recipient list is 2026 events (announced Jan 17, 2026); per-award amounts were not published for 2026 or 2024, only for 2025 (CERC minutes). A 2027 cycle ($90,000) was approved Sept 24, 2026 but the awardee page could not be fetched. Recurring recipients across cycles: Rainbow Center/Tacoma Pride, Tacoma Light Trail, Proctor Arts Fest, Asia Pacific Cultural Center, WayOut Kids Juneteenth, Write253 Wayzgoose, Tacoma Porchfest, Tacoma Art Museum Dia de los Muertos, Museum of Glass Glass Fest. Events must be free, all-ages and in Tacoma.

Pierce County Tourism Promotion Area (TP.notes: Pierce County publishes TPA 'funded programs' documents by fiscal year, but every year found (FY2022, FY2024, FY2025, FY2026) lists one recipient: the county CVB (Travel Tacoma) for a combined tourism and sports marketing program. The Event Marketing and Sports Event Marketing categories first appear as separately pooled line items for the 2027 cycle (Event Marketing $42,950 pool; Sports Event Marketing $55,500 pool; scoring requires 300 peak / 500 total room nights for Event Marketing and 200 room nights per event for Sports). The 2027 awards were on the Aug 19, 2026 TPA Commission agenda ('2027 Grant Awarding Decisions') but no award list or minutes with recipients were posted. TPAC agendas reference 'recipient quarterly reports' but do not name recipients. No per-event TPA award to a festival or sports event could be verified. The county's separate Lodging Tax program (up to $5.5M for 2027, categories including New Event Development and Existing Event Marketing & Operations) does publish per-event awards; three FY2026 LTAC event awards are included above and flagged as non-TPA.

Tacoma Creates Impact Funding.notes: The city announces funded organizations by name only. Per-organization amounts and the Impact Level A / Level B / Comprehensive split are not published in press releases, TCAB minutes, or guidelines; TCAB minutes (June 2, 2025) only confirm notifications went out. The 40 orgs listed are the first half (alphabetical) of the 80 funded for 2026-27; the other 40 are: Tacoma City Ballet, Tacoma Community Boat Builders, Tacoma Concert Band, Tacoma Fun Parade, Tacoma Historical Society, Tacoma Little Theatre, Tacoma Music Academy, Tacoma Music Collaborative, Tacoma Musical Playhouse, Tacoma Opera, Tacoma Photo Center, Tacoma Puzzle Hunt, Tacoma Refugee Choir, Tacoma Sister Cities, Tacoma Tree Foundation, Tacoma Youth Symphony Association, Tacoma Youth Theatre, Tahoma Indian Center, Ted Brown Music Outreach, The Grand Cinema, The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra, The Night Media Foundation, The Puget Sounds, Toolbox Learning Laboratories, Vision253, WayOut Kids, World Affairs Council of Tacoma, Write253, Mo' Motion Dance, Momentum Musician LLC, Northwest Repertory Singers, Oasis Youth Center, One Table Show, Pacific Northwest Dance Foundation, Queer NW, Remakery, Screaming Butterflies Theatre, Second Cycle Community Cycle Center, Southeast Asian Comedy Collective, Swan Creek Art Academy. Eligibility requires a Tacoma business address (limited Pierce County exception for orgs delivering 75%+ programming in Tacoma) and a primary purpose of arts, culture, heritage or science. Average award across all categories is roughly $80,000 but that is skewed by large Comprehensive awards to museums and theaters.

Snohomish County Tourism Promotion Area.notes: Snohomish County posts year-by-year TPA project lists (2023, 2024, 2025); 2025 is the latest, updated Aug 1, 2025 so late-2025 awards may be missing. No 2026 list was posted as of Oct 30, 2026; 2026 board minutes are hosted on a squarespace subdomain that could not be fetched. 2024 list also included a $5,000 RRC Associates study (omitted above). 2023 list totals do not reconcile ($562,350 listed vs $410,850 stated); 2023 awards included IIHF U18 Women's Championship $100,000, Spartan Race $75,000, NW Aerials $40,000, WIAA Volleyball $40,000, US Pro Gymnastics $40,450, Everett 3on3 $35,000, Snohomish Running Co. $30,000. Spectator events with hotel-night draw (Spartan Race, Everett 3on3, Cruizin to Colby, Everett Pride, GeekFest, MACFest, Women's Run) are funded every year. City of Lynnwood itself received $25,000 (2025, Best Bites) and $50,800 (2024, light rail marketing). Purpose is overnight stays; applications go through the county Jotform and the TPA Advisory Board recommends to County Council. Separate county Hotel-Motel (lodging tax) small fund averages $10,000 per award, $5,000-$50,000 range.

Jan 2026 Arts Commission summary: $10,000 allocated for other art projects in 2026 and a $100,000 request for the 2027-2028 budget split evenly between a utility-box art program and the Creative Arts Grant program (pending council), implying roughly $50,000/biennium for grants. Eligible events must be free, open to the public, in Lynnwood city limits, and expected to serve 250+ people.
Lynnwood Event Partnership (Community Ev.notes: The city publishes no list of partnered events or what each received. The program page states the Community Event Collaboration Grant's cash funding is suspended because of city budget constraints; only the in-kind Event Partnership benefits remain, applied for via an online form (contact Events@lynnwoodwa.gov, 425-670-5504). The related Healthy Lynnwood mini-grant (community arts projects, 1:1 match, rolling reviews March/June/September) is marked GRANTS CLOSED with no recipients published. The city's own produced events (CELEBRATE! music festival ~2,500 attendance, Fair on 44th ~3,000, Paws in the Park, Sandlot Cinemas, Shakespeare in the Park) are listed on the Event Sponsorships page, where the city seeks sponsors starting at $300; those are city events, not partnership grantees. For cash support for a Lynnwood event, the Snohomish County TPA (City of Lynnwood received $25,000 in 2025 and $50,800 in 2024) and county Hotel-Motel fund are the active channels.
